artists.biography: Easy Star All-Stars is a reggae collective with a rotating roster of musicians and singers founded by the co-founders (Michael Goldwasser, Eric Smith, Lem Oppenheimer & Remy Gerstein) of New York City-based Easy Star Records in 1997. They originally formed as a studio band for the label's earliest recordings. Although they have backed many artists[who?] and produced several original releases, they are best known for covering popular albums in a reggae and dub style and have released four cover albums to date. The first, released in 2003, was an interpretation of Pink Floyd's classic The Dark Side of the Moon entitled Dub Side of the Moon; the second was 2006's Radiodread, a song-by-song cover of Radiohead's OK Computer. In April 2009, they released a cover of The Beatles' Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band entitled Easy Star's Lonely Hearts Dub Band. In 2012, Easy Star's Thrillah was released, a cover of Michael Jackson's classic album. In March 2008 they released an EP consisting mostly of non-cover material. On 5 April 2011, they released their first original album entitled First Light.

perplexity.description:
Radiodread, released in 2006 by Easy Star All-Stars on Easy Star Records, is a reggae reinterpretation of Radiohead’s landmark 1997 album OK Computer. The album transforms the original’s brooding art-rock soundscapes into lush, dub-infused reggae arrangements, showcasing the collective’s signature ability to reimagine classic rock albums within a Caribbean musical framework. Featuring guest appearances from notable artists such as Toots & The Maytals, Citizen Cope, Horace Andy, and Morgan Heritage, Radiodread stands out for its ambitious production and genre-blending creativity.

As the follow-up to their acclaimed Dub Side of the Moon (2003), Radiodread further established Easy Star All-Stars as pioneers in the field of reggae tribute albums. The project is widely regarded as one of their most accomplished works, praised for its respectful yet inventive approach to the source material. Critics lauded the album for feeling less like a mere covers record and more like a lost reggae classic, with outlets such as Entertainment Weekly, All Music Guide, and the LA Times highlighting its sincerity, originality, and artistic merit. The album’s reception was further validated when Radiohead’s Thom Yorke publicly commended the project from the stage.
